arguments.literal: Absence of a durable ticket neither requires nor authorises creating one. An exact product-authorised work instruction may supply the upstream work authority for a one-run contract; a generic request or a model-widened scope cannot. A durable ticket is created or updated only when the selection table requires surviving state and the actor holds ticket-state authority. An explicit instruction from ticket-state authority to create a durable record selects that durability; it does not admit an execution contract or widen its upstream work authority.
P6, P2

Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis. Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy. A ticket's active status, its lane, or an admitted or retained contract is never the admission of a growth basis.
P6, P2

The admitted contract names one durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and residual obligation is recorded there before return; a conversation return alone is not durable evidence; if no such surface is authorised and available, admission refuses.
P4b

The admitted result identifies the admission mechanism and its authority, the exact contract identity or digest, the decision and the evidence, including any human override; absent those coordinates the contract stays drafted or rejected. Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority its owner has not admitted.
P6, P2

The admission mechanism and the durable result and evidence surface are the ones the product definition binds. When that surface is the ticket or the sprint manifest, the admitted result with its coordinates is recorded there. A carrier's lane, status or prose that asserts admission without those coordinates is not admission evidence, and the contract it describes remains drafted or rejected.
P6, P4b

A ticket, a sprint entry or a drafted work contract is an admission candidate, never automatic truth; the contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded. An admitted execution contract should be logged in runtime and event truth, available to prompt assembly, and available to later closure checking, so that execution and closure read the same admitted basis.
P6, P4b

The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime: a durable ticket where the work needs identity across sessions; a sprint-local entry where its only value is traceability inside a batch; a run or return record (the rc.2 run-scoped execution contract) where the work lives and dies with one activation. The triage fields are required wherever substantive work begins; a ticket per change is not.
Standing: conserves the TICKET core model's selection of the smallest lawful carrier; reframes its default, so that no carrier is the default and the triage fields are the required minimum.

Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream work authority, then select the first matching row. For work inside an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it is the current run. Rows (condition -> execution-contract source; durable-ticket decision): (1) no applicable upstream work authority exists -> no execution contract is admitted; do not create a ticket as substitute authority, stop or re-enter. (2) authority exists and an existing admitted ticket covers the exact work -> derive the run-scoped contract from that ticket; reuse it, do not create another ticket. (3) authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work or an open obligation needs independent state beyond the local carrier boundary -> one durable ticket plus the run-scoped contract; create or update the ticket only under ticket-state authority. (4) authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work stays inside one admitted sprint with no state required after sprint close -> the sprint manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry; no durable ticket. (5) authority exists, no exact admitted ticket or sprint covers the work, and the work ends in the current run with no independent surviving state -> an intake-drafted run-scoped contract; no durable ticket.
P2, P4b, P6

The drafting actor never infers admission from its own draft, from the presence of a carrier (ticket, sprint entry, work contract), from lane placement or from an active label. Prose asserting admission is not admission evidence; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution basis.
P6

Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied. A contract is in one of the states drafted, admitted, rejected or superseded.
P6
Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an explicit human override of the exact contract. Absent or rejected admission returns the missing work authority without execution.
P6

Tickets are durable work authority. An execution contract is the run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a ticket, from a sprint manifest plus an included ticket or iteration entry, or drafted during intake when no durable or sprint-local work identity is required. A ticket survives sessions and work waves; a sprint survives one bounded execution batch and its close review; an execution contract is the current admitted execution function for one run. Execution contracts are not a rival backlog or a second planning surface.
P0, P3

Work arrives; the system selects the smallest lawful work carrier for its required lifetime; an agent drafts one run-scoped execution contract from that carrier; the system validates and admits or rejects the contract; execution may proceed in the same invocation under the admitted contract; closure is checked against that same contract. Execution and closure use the same admitted categorisation, criteria, proof surface and non-closure conditions; the resulting state still flows through proof, gap analysis and repricing.
P6, P2
No universal quota, ticket count, actor count or accounting carrier follows from the cost rule.
An obligation with no route to the selected outcome is unjustified.
A selected outcome defines adequacy; interfaces inherit material obligations from the transformation they serve.
Standing: independent. Identical capacity serves opposite purposes.

Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced; an obligation, distinction, carrier or document is justified when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space pays for the concepts, joins, exceptions and states an actor must hold to decide.

When admission is absent or rejected, ACTIVATION section 1 returns the missing work authority without execution. Before that return, an obligation that must survive the run becomes a sprint-local entry when its lifetime stays inside the admitted sprint; otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket, only under ticket-state authority; where that authority is absent, it is retained in the contract's named durable result and evidence surface or in an already-authorised enclosing carrier, closure is marked withheld on ticket-state authority, and the required re-entry is returned.
P4b, P6

"Ticket-shaped" describes the categorisation, closure criteria, proof surface, non-closure conditions and the other required execution-contract fields. It creates no durable ticket identity and no ticket-lane state.
P3

Absence of a durable ticket neither requires nor authorises creating one. An exact product-authorised work instruction may supply the upstream work authority for a one-run contract; a generic request or a model-widened scope cannot. A durable ticket is created or updated only when the selection table requires surviving state and the actor holds ticket-state authority. An explicit instruction from ticket-state authority to create a durable record selects that durability; it does not admit an execution contract or widen its upstream work authority.
P6, P2

residuals.detail: PROFILES section 3 conserves DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD by reference, which requires the ontology-first derivation chain where it applies, while ACTIVATION section 6 asks every obligation to pay for the ambiguity it removes. Whether a design boundary with no material alternative must still pay the full chain is not decided by this corpus; it is a question for the profile's owner.

Each independent commitment carries a one-sentence non-entailment argument in its qualification. These are claims of independence with an informal witness each; none is formalised and P4a states none. The accepted C1 realisation argues them at greater length; the standard conserves only the sentence.

symbols.label: Admission: the relation that validates a drafted step contract against its cited basis and admits it for execution; distinct from drafting even inside one invocation
Allowance: declared resource bound and spend measurement where capability fit or cost is the governed question
Carrier of a work item: durable ticket, sprint-local entry, or run or return record
Constructor: the relation that produces the candidate and self-review
Contract state: drafted, admitted, rejected or superseded
Execution contract: the run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a ticket, from a sprint manifest plus an included entry, or drafted during intake
Local carrier boundary: the admitted sprint for work inside it, otherwise the current run
P1 Interpretation
P2 Purpose
P3 Identity
P4a Typed composition
P6 Justification and authority
Proportionality: the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced
Software design profile: binds the ontology-first derivation chain and the design laws
Step: one bounded unit of work (intake, selected context, grant, execution, output); the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active frame configuration, on an exact subject
Step-produced fact: a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; a reproducible observation is not one
Ticket-state authority: the authority under which a durable ticket may be created or updated
Intake triage: change intent, class, re-entry point and when triage occurred
Upstream work authority: the applicable authority for the work, established before any carrier is selected; its absence admits no execution contract
Work wave: the current bounded selection of outcome-bearing work
